label: History
value: Anne Shirley was born in Bolingbroke, Nova Scotia.
unit: Born in Bolingbroke, Nova Scotia, Anne Shirley spent her early years as an orphan living with Mrs. Thomas, Mrs. Hammond, and at an asylum before being brought to Green Gables in Avonlea by Matthew Cuthbert. Although Marilla Cuthbert initially intended to send her back because they had requested a boy, Marilla and Matthew ultimately decided to keep and raise her. Anne quickly formed a deep bond with Diana Barry and entered a fierce academic rivalry with Gilbert Blythe after he pulled her braid at school. After completing her studies at Queen's Academy and winning the Avery scholarship, Anne chose to forfeit the scholarship to stay at Green Gables and teach locally after Matthew died and Marilla faced failing eyesight. During her time teaching, she joined with friends to organize the Avonlea Village Improvement Society, unintentionally sold her neighbor Mr. Harrison's cow before befriending him, and took in the orphaned Keith twins, Davy and Dora, with Marilla. Later, Anne attended Redmond College in Kingsport, renting a house named Patty's Place with her friends and Aunt Jamesina, and inherited a thousand dollars from Miss Josephine Barry. Throughout her college years, she refused proposals from Billy Andrews, Charlie Sloane, and Roy Gardner, and initially turned down Gilbert Blythe before realizing her true feelings for him. After returning home following graduation, Anne visited Hester Gray's garden with Gilbert, where she accepted his proposal of marriage.

unit: Born in Bolingbroke, Nova Scotia, Anne Shirley spent her early years as an orphan living with Mrs. Thomas, Mrs. Hammond, and at an asylum before being brought to Green Gables in Avonlea by Matthew Cuthbert. Although Marilla Cuthbert initially intended to send her back because they had requested a boy, Marilla and Matthew ultimately decided to keep and raise her. Anne quickly formed a deep bond with Diana Barry and entered a fierce academic rivalry with Gilbert Blythe after he pulled her braid at school. After completing her studies at Queen's Academy and winning the Avery scholarship, Anne chose to forfeit the scholarship to stay at Green Gables and teach locally after Matthew died and Marilla faced failing eyesight. During her time teaching, she joined with friends to organize the Avonlea Village Improvement Society, unintentionally sold her neighbor Mr. Harrison's cow before befriending him, and took in the orphaned Keith twins, Davy and Dora, with Marilla. Later, Anne attended Redmond College in Kingsport, renting a house named Patty's Place with her friends and Aunt Jamesina, and inherited a thousand dollars from Miss Josephine Barry. Throughout her college years, she refused proposals from Billy Andrews, Charlie Sloane, and Roy Gardner, and initially turned down Gilbert Blythe before realizing her true feelings for him. After returning home following graduation, Anne visited Hester Gray's garden with Gilbert, where she accepted his proposal of marriage.

value: Anne Shirley said: "I love pretty things; and I hate to look in the glass and see something that isn’t pretty. It makes me feel so sorrowful—just as I feel when I look at any ugly thing. I pity it because it isn’t beautiful."

label: History
value: Aunt Jamesina was named after James.
unit: Aunt Jamesina was named after her father, James, who drowned at sea shortly before her birth. Throughout her life, her mother and husband prevented her from owning a yellow silk dress, and she eventually raised a daughter whom she taught to cook before sending her to college. Later in life, she accepted a cat named Sarah from her washerwoman and took up residence at Patty's Place along with Sarah and another cat named Joseph to chaperone Anne Shirley and her college friends. During her time living at Patty's Place, she maintained a relaxed attitude toward the girls' independence, managed household chats, and shared her humorous views on life and suitors. Over the next four years, she remained at the house, sharing stories and laughs with the girls as they completed their studies at Redmond College up until their graduation.

value: Aunt Jamesina said: "Kittens have to be drowned, I admit, or the world would be overrun. But no decent, grown-up cat should be done to death—unless he sucks eggs."

label: Quote
value: Aunt Jamesina said: "Well, I hope so, Anne. I do hope so, because I love her. But I can’t understand her—she beats me. She isn’t like any of the girls I ever knew, or any of the girls I was myself."

label: Quote
value: Aunt Jamesina said: "Yes, in my soul. But I’ll admit my legs aren’t as young as yours. You go and get some fresh air, Anne. You look pale lately."

label: Quote
value: Aunt Jamesina said: "Anybody is liable to rheumatism in her legs, Anne. It’s only old people who should have rheumatism in their souls, though. Thank goodness, I never have. When you get rheumatism in your soul you might as well go and pick out your coffin."

label: Quote
value: Aunt Jamesina said: "I’ve got them yet. There are three old widowers at home who have been casting sheep’s eyes at me for some time. You children needn’t think you own all the romance in the world."

label: Personality
value: Davy Keith is a mischievous child.
unit: Davy Keith is a mischievous and disobedient child, often given to making terrible faces, yet he possesses a natural knack for winning love. Highly inquisitive, curious, and practical, he lacks imagination and frequently asks questions that can unnerve others. Though heedless and forgetful, he can display great energetic zeal, and he is described as a reformed character. Sorrow is easily comforted in him by food like plum jam. His ambitions include becoming a storekeeper to keep candy and bananas, and he wants to live to be a hundred years old.

label: History
value: Davy Keith lost his father as an infant.
unit: Davy Keith lost his father as an infant and was brought up without proper guidance before Marilla Cuthbert brought him and his twin sister, Dora, to live at Green Gables. A naturally mischievous boy, Davy quickly got into trouble by putting a toad in Marilla's bed and later locking Dora in a toolhouse. When confronted by Anne Shirley, Davy tearfully promised never to lie again after seeing that he had made her cry. Over time, Marilla and Anne developed a deep affection for Davy despite his constant antics, recognizing his need for direction. Following the death of Richard Keith, money was left in trust for the twins, ensuring they could permanently remain at Green Gables. As Anne grew older and left for Redmond College, Davy frequently sent her letters and confessed his moral struggles and misdeeds to her when she returned home on visits. During one holiday break, Davy convinced Dora to skip Sunday School to go fishing, but later confessed his lying to Anne and sought forgiveness. He continued to keep Anne updated on his schoolwork and antics during her stays at home, and eventually broke the news to her that Gilbert Blythe was critically ill with typhoid fever.

label: Quote
value: Davy Keith said: "I just did it for fun. Things have been so awful quiet here for so long that I thought it would be fun to give you folks a big scare. It was, too."

label: Quote
value: Davy Keith said: “I never will, now that I know it’s bad,” asseverated Davy between sobs. “If you ever catch me telling a whopper again you can . . .” Davy groped mentally for a suitable penance . . . “you can skin me alive, Anne.”

label: Quote
value: Davy Keith said: “Why?” queried Davy, settling comfortably down and looking up with a tearstained, investigating face. “Why ain’t whopper as good as falsehood? I want to know. It’s just as big a word.”

label: Quote
value: Davy Keith said: “Then,” said Davy decidedly, “Marilla is bad, for she tells them. And she’s worse’n me, for I didn’t know it was wrong but she does.”

label: Quote
value: Davy Keith said: “But I tell you there is,” persisted Davy. “It was in that question Marilla taught me last Sunday. ‘Why should we love God?’ It says, ‘Because He makes preserves, and redeems us.’ Preserves is just a holy way of saying jam.”

label: Quote
value: Diana Barry said: "I’m awfully glad you’ve come to live at Green Gables. It will be jolly to have somebody to play with. There isn’t any other girl who lives near enough to play with, and I’ve no sisters big enough."

label: Quote
value: Diana Barry said: "Why, he makes fun of all the girls. He laughs at mine because it’s so black. He’s called me a crow a dozen times; and I never heard him apologize for anything before, either."

label: Quote
value: Diana Barry said: "I do think you’re mean. What shall I do? Mr. Phillips will make me sit with that horrid Gertie Pye—I know he will because she is sitting alone. Do come back, Anne."

label: Quote
value: Diana Barry said: “I don’t believe he’ll find the doctor at Carmody,” sobbed Diana. “I know that Dr. Blair went to town and I guess Dr. Spencer would go too. Young Mary Joe never saw anybody with croup and Mrs. Lynde is away. Oh, Anne!”

label: Quote
value: Diana Barry said: "I guess we must have made as much as ten dollars. Mind you, Mr. Allan is going to send an account of it to the Charlottetown papers."

value: Dora is a quiet child.
unit: Dora is a quiet, lovely, and well-behaved child described as being very good, faithful, and neat. Characterized by her prim and proper demeanor, she comports herself like a model child by speaking demurely when addressed and maintaining silence otherwise. She is industrious, observant, and systematic, never needing to be told how to do a task twice and never forgetting her duties. Highly composed and placid, it takes a great deal to ruffle her composure even at eight years old, though her predictable nature is sometimes considered monotonous.

label: History
value: Dora Keith was brought to live at Green Gables by Marilla.
unit: Dora Keith was brought to live at Green Gables by Marilla alongside her twin brother Davy, though Davy's unruly behavior soon caused Dora to fall into a pigpen. Shortly after her arrival, Dora went missing and was found locked inside Mr. Harrison's toolhouse by her brother. Considered quiet and well-behaved by Marilla and Anne, Dora was frightened at school by ghost stories told by a classmate. Following the death of Richard Keith, money was left in trust to secure Dora and Davy's permanent residence at Green Gables. Later, Davy convinced Dora to skip Sunday School with him to go fishing instead.

label: History
value: Gilbert Blythe spent three years in Alberta caring for his sick father.
unit: Gilbert Blythe spent three years in Alberta caring for his sick father and a summer visiting cousins in New Brunswick before returning home to Avonlea. Upon returning to school, he inadvertently sparked a fierce, years-long academic rivalry with Anne Shirley after mockingly calling her 'Carrots' and pulling her braid, prompting her to smash a slate over his head and refuse his apology. Though Anne maintained a bitter front, Gilbert repeatedly attempted to make amends, even rescueing her when her boat sank. The two continued to compete intensely through their studies in Avonlea and Queen's Academy, where Gilbert earned the graduation medal. Demonstrating his underlying kindness, he surrendered his appointment as the Avonlea schoolteacher so Anne could remain near Green Gables, an act that finally prompted her to forgive him and become his close friend. Alongside Anne, Gilbert co-founded the Avonlea Village Improvement Society, and after two years of teaching, both moved on to attend Redmond College in Kingsport. There, he led the freshman class to victory in the annual Arts Rush. During their second year, Gilbert proposed to Anne in an orchard, but she rejected him, fracturing their close friendship and leaving him heartbroken. Over time, he began spending time with Christine Stuart, which secretly disquieted Anne, though he eventually accompanied Anne back home following Diana's wedding. Shortly after, Gilbert contracted a severe case of typhoid fever, passing a critical night before recovering. Upon his recovery, he took Anne for a walk to Hester Gray's garden, where he proposed once again; this time, Anne happily accepted, and the two looked forward to a future together.

Upon returning to school, he inadvertently sparked a fierce, years-long academic rivalry with Anne Shirley after mockingly calling her 'Carrots' and pulling her braid, prompting her to smash a slate over his head and refuse his apology. Though Anne maintained a bitter front, Gilbert repeatedly attempted to make amends, even rescueing her when her boat sank. The two continued to compete intensely through their studies in Avonlea and Queen's Academy, where Gilbert earned the graduation medal. Demonstrating his underlying kindness, he surrendered his appointment as the Avonlea schoolteacher so Anne could remain near Green Gables, an act that finally prompted her to forgive him and become his close friend. Alongside Anne, Gilbert co-founded the Avonlea Village Improvement Society, and after two years of teaching, both moved on to attend Redmond College in Kingsport. There, he led the freshman class to victory in the annual Arts Rush. During their second year, Gilbert proposed to Anne in an orchard, but she rejected him, fracturing their close friendship and leaving him heartbroken. Over time, he began spending time with Christine Stuart, which secretly disquieted Anne, though he eventually accompanied Anne back home following Diana's wedding. Shortly after, Gilbert contracted a severe case of typhoid fever, passing a critical night before recovering. Upon his recovery, he took Anne for a walk to Hester Gray's garden, where he proposed once again; this time, Anne happily accepted, and the two looked forward to a future together.

unit: Gilbert Blythe spent three years in Alberta caring for his sick father and a summer visiting cousins in New Brunswick before returning home to Avonlea. Upon returning to school, he inadvertently sparked a fierce, years-long academic rivalry with Anne Shirley after mockingly calling her 'Carrots' and pulling her braid, prompting her to smash a slate over his head and refuse his apology. Though Anne maintained a bitter front, Gilbert repeatedly attempted to make amends, even rescueing her when her boat sank. The two continued to compete intensely through their studies in Avonlea and Queen's Academy, where Gilbert earned the graduation medal. Demonstrating his underlying kindness, he surrendered his appointment as the Avonlea schoolteacher so Anne could remain near Green Gables, an act that finally prompted her to forgive him and become his close friend. Alongside Anne, Gilbert co-founded the Avonlea Village Improvement Society, and after two years of teaching, both moved on to attend Redmond College in Kingsport. There, he led the freshman class to victory in the annual Arts Rush. During their second year, Gilbert proposed to Anne in an orchard, but she rejected him, fracturing their close friendship and leaving him heartbroken. Over time, he began spending time with Christine Stuart, which secretly disquieted Anne, though he eventually accompanied Anne back home following Diana's wedding. Shortly after, Gilbert contracted a severe case of typhoid fever, passing a critical night before recovering. Upon his recovery, he took Anne for a walk to Hester Gray's garden, where he proposed once again; this time, Anne happily accepted, and the two looked forward to a future together.

value: Gilbert Blythe said: "It wasn’t particularly good of me at all, Anne. I was pleased to be able to do you some small service. Are we going to be friends after this? Have you really forgiven me my old fault?"

value: Gilbert Blythe said: “Not she,” said Gilbert emphatically. “I know Louisa Spencer well. She doesn’t ‘believe’ in Village Improvement Societies, but she does believe in dollars and cents. She’d be more likely to urge Judson on than to dissuade him.”

value: Harrison is fussy.
unit: Harrison is a fussy, fidgety, and middle-aged man who has earned a reputation for being an odd crank. Though he prides himself on his outspokenness, which others can find trying, he maintains an outwardly sympathetic and kind nature. He routinely smokes a pipe on his veranda and holds a prejudice against marriage, though he is later described as a changed and much nicer man after remarrying. He is also fastidious and hard to please when reviewing written work.

label: History
value: Before settling in Avonlea, Harrison lived in Scottsford, New Brunswick.
unit: Before settling in Avonlea, Harrison lived in Scottsford, New Brunswick, having visited Prince Edward Island as a boy. Following a promise made to his dying sister, he married Emily Scott and took a fortnight's wedding trip to St. John, though he later kept a bachelor's hall after his sister passed away. Upon moving to Avonlea as Anne Shirley's neighbor, he initially confronted her angrily when a cow broke into his oatfield, but the two formed an unexpected friendship after Anne accidentally sold his Jersey cow and came to his house with a cake and money to confess. Over time, Harrison offered his opinions on Anne's teaching methods, discussed village news, and survived a severe storm that tragically killed his parrot, Ginger. Eventually, Harrison explained the history of his marriage and past falling out to Anne, leading to his reunion with his wife Emily. Harrison continued to support Anne's endeavors, providing feedback on her story Averil's Atonement, encouraging her to keep writing despite early magazine rejections, and delivering her mail during a stormy winter holiday.

label: Quote
value: Harrison said: "Sorry, miss! Sorry isn’t going to help matters any. You’d better go and look at the havoc that animal has made in my oats . . . trampled them from center to circumference, miss."

label: Quote
value: Harrison said: “Who? Mrs. Lynde? Don’t you tell me I’m like that old gossip,” said Mr. Harrison irritably. “I’m not . . . not a bit. What have you got in that box?”

label: Quote
value: Harrison said: "I don’t, that’s a fact, and I’m mighty fond of it, too. I’m much obliged to you. It looks good on top. I hope it’s good all the way through."

label: Quote
value: Harrison said: "Well, I’ll tell you what, miss, you must help me eat it. I’ll put the kettle on and we’ll have a cup of tea. How will that do?"

label: Quote
value: Harrison said: "I see you haven’t much confidence in my ability to make tea. You’re wrong . . . I can brew up as good a jorum of tea as you ever drank. But go ahead yourself. Fortunately it rained last Sunday, so there’s plenty of clean dishes."

label: Personality
value: Jane Andrews is described as a plain individual.
unit: Jane Andrews is described as a plain, steady, and sensible individual whose unflappable nature keeps her from being easily rattled. She possesses a lady-like, neat, and practical demeanor, working as a conscientious and plodding student who earned honors in domestic science for her strong cooking abilities. Although she originally aimed to study for Queen's Entrance examination and envisioned devoting her entire life to teaching, she eventually resigns from the Avonlea school to head West in the fall. As a teacher, her strict approach of punishing pupils for funny speeches makes the work monotonous, even though she strives to earn her salary fairly, satisfy the trustees, and secure a place on the School Inspector's roll of honor. Now engaged to a millionaire, her main difficulty is that her husband will not allow her to cook despite her high skill in it.

label: History
value: Janet Sweet lost her sister Anne when she was young.
unit: Janet Sweet, who lost her sister Anne when she was young, worked as a pleasant landlady at Wayside, where she befriended her boarder Anne. After twenty years of silent courtship from her admirer John Douglas, Janet took Anne's advice to take a firm stand and sharply rejected his escort after a prayer meeting, though Anne quickly rushed to reconcile the pair. Following the eventual death of John's mother, John proposed to Janet, revealing he had been bound by a promise to his mother to wait until after her passing before marrying or telling anyone.

value: Janet said: "If she wasn’t—but she is. So we mustn’t speak evil of her. But I’m happy at last, Anne. And I wouldn’t have minded waiting so long a bit if I’d only known why."

label: Quote
value: Janet said: "Oh, she does. She’s told me time and again that she’d love to see John settled before her time comes. She’s always giving him hints—you heard her yourself the other day. I thought I’d ha’ gone through the floor."

label: Quote
value: Janet said: “I couldn’t,” said poor Janet pathetically. “You see, Anne, I’ve always been awful fond of John. He might just as well keep coming as not, for there was never anybody else I’d want, so it didn’t matter.”

label: Quote
value: Janet said: "No, I guess not. I was afraid to try, anyway, for fear he’d think I meant it and just go. I suppose I’m a poor-spirited creature, but that is how I feel. And I can’t help it."

label: Quote
value: Janet said: “I dunno,” said Janet hopelessly. “I dunno if I could ever get up enough spunk. Things have drifted so long. But I’ll think it over.”

label: History
value: Lavendar Lewis lived at Echo Lodge
unit: Miss Lavendar Lewis lived at Echo Lodge alongside her young maid, Charlotta the Fourth, where she eventually met Anne Shirley and Diana Barry when they stumbled upon her home and joined her for tea. Over subsequent visits, she shared the story of her past romance and quarrel with Stephen Irving, and she soon formed a fond friendship with Stephen's son, Paul. After experiencing a period of despondency, she received a note from Stephen via Anne, leading to his arrival at Echo Lodge and their reconciliation. The two were subsequently married in an intimate garden ceremony at Echo Lodge before departing. Later, during a summer vacation visit, Anne confided in Miss Lavendar that she had refused Gilbert Blythe's marriage proposal because she viewed him only as a friend.

label: Quote
value: Lavendar Lewis said: "But oh, won’t you stay and have tea with me? Please, do. Mr. Kimball’s will have tea over before you get there. And Charlotta the Fourth and I will be so glad to have you."

label: Quote
value: Lavendar Lewis said: "to believe I’m old. Now, who are you . . . just for convenience’ sake? Diana Barry? And Anne Shirley? May I pretend that I’ve known you for a hundred years and call you Anne and Diana right away?"

label: Quote
value: Lavendar Lewis said: "I love them myself. They are very good company . . . with a little pretending. On calm evenings Charlotta the Fourth and I often sit out here and amuse ourselves with them. Charlotta, take back the horn and hang it carefully in its place."

label: Quote
value: Lavendar Lewis said: "It gave me a shock to hear about Stephen’s son that first day you were here, Anne. I’ve never been able to mention him to you since, but I’ve wanted to know all about him. What sort of a boy is he?"

label: Quote
value: Lavendar Lewis said: "Oh, I’m not so old as I thought . . . and I don’t need a single blue pill! Girls, when you come back with your strawberries we’ll have tea out here under the silver poplar. I’ll have it all ready for you with home-grown cream."

value: Marilla Cuthbert said: “There, there, Marilla, you can have your own way,” said Matthew reassuringly. “Only be as good and kind to her as you can without spoiling her. I kind of think she’s one of the sort you can do anything with if you only get her to love you.”

label: Quote
value: Marilla Cuthbert said: "Matthew Cuthbert, I’m astonished at you. You know that Anne’s behavior was dreadful, and yet you take her part! I suppose you’ll be saying next thing that she oughtn’t to be punished at all!"

label: Quote
value: Marilla Cuthbert said: "She’ll have her meals regular, and I’ll carry them up to her myself. But she’ll stay up there until she’s willing to apologize to Mrs. Lynde, and that’s final, Matthew."

label: Quote
value: Marilla Cuthbert said: "and I can’t prevent her, for her father aids and abets her. She’s always poring over a book. I’m glad she has the prospect of a playmate—perhaps it will take her more out-of-doors."

value: Marilla Cuthbert said: “I’ll go and have another look,” said Marilla, determining to be just. “If you put that brooch back it’s there still. If it isn’t I’ll know you didn’t, that’s all!”

label: History
value: Matthew Cuthbert lived at Green Gables.
unit: Matthew Cuthbert, an extremely shy man who lived at Green Gables, had worn a full soft brown beard since age twenty and generally dreaded all women except his sister Marilla and Mrs. Rachel Lynde. Despite his usual reluctance to leave home, he drove to Bright River station expecting to collect an orphan boy to help on the farm, only to find a talkative young girl named Anne Shirley instead. Although Marilla initially wanted to return the child, Matthew gently advocated for keeping her. He grew deeply fond of Anne, secretly persuading her to apologize to Mrs. Lynde after a quarrel, bringing her sweeties, and giving her a calf he bought from Mr. Bell. He consistently encouraged her pursuits, convincing Marilla to let her attend a local concert and later enduring an embarrassing attempt at a store before enlisting Mrs. Lynde's help to procure a stylish brown dress with puffed sleeves for Anne's Christmas gift. As Anne matured and succeeded academically, Matthew proudly shared in her achievements, including her entrance into Queen's Academy and her winning of the Avery Scholarship. Following her return home from academy commencement, Anne noticed his failing health during a memorable evening walk. Shortly thereafter, Matthew collapsed and died suddenly upon reading news of a bank failure.

Despite his usual reluctance to leave home, he drove to Bright River station expecting to collect an orphan boy to help on the farm, only to find a talkative young girl named Anne Shirley instead. Although Marilla initially wanted to return the child, Matthew gently advocated for keeping her. He grew deeply fond of Anne, secretly persuading her to apologize to Mrs. Lynde after a quarrel, bringing her sweeties, and giving her a calf he bought from Mr. Bell. He consistently encouraged her pursuits, convincing Marilla to let her attend a local concert and later enduring an embarrassing attempt at a store before enlisting Mrs. Lynde's help to procure a stylish brown dress with puffed sleeves for Anne's Christmas gift. As Anne matured and succeeded academically, Matthew proudly shared in her achievements, including her entrance into Queen's Academy and her winning of the Avery Scholarship. Following her return home from academy commencement, Anne noticed his failing health during a memorable evening walk. Shortly thereafter, Matthew collapsed and died suddenly upon reading news of a bank failure.

label: History
value: Paul Irving is an imaginative student
unit: Paul Irving is an imaginative student whose mother died three years prior to his time at the Avonlea school. On his teacher Anne's first day, he cheered her up by gifting her wild orchids, and he later shared written compositions detailing his fantastical imaginary friends. During a walk, Paul shared his thoughts with Anne about his parents, and the two later enjoyed tea together as they discussed his childhood worries and active imagination. When Anne announced her resignation to attend college, Paul was left distressed by the news. Shortly before Anne's departure, Paul accompanied her to Echo Lodge, where he bonded with Miss Lavendar over their shared experiences with imaginary dream-people. After his father, Stephen Irving, returned and reunited with Miss Lavendar, Paul expressed excitement about their upcoming wedding and his planned move to Boston.

On his teacher Anne's first day, he cheered her up by gifting her wild orchids, and he later shared written compositions detailing his fantastical imaginary friends. During a walk, Paul shared his thoughts with Anne about his parents, and the two later enjoyed tea together as they discussed his childhood worries and active imagination. When Anne announced her resignation to attend college, Paul was left distressed by the news. Shortly before Anne's departure, Paul accompanied her to Echo Lodge, where he bonded with Miss Lavendar over their shared experiences with imaginary dream-people. After his father, Stephen Irving, returned and reunited with Miss Lavendar, Paul expressed excitement about their upcoming wedding and his planned move to Boston.

value: Paul Irving said: "I’ve eaten enough to make anyone grow. I do hope, now that I’ve begun, I’ll keep on till I’m as tall as father. He is six feet, you know, Miss Lavendar."

label: Quote

label: History
value: Phil Gordon is the daughter of a prominent man from an old Bluenose family.
unit: Phil Gordon, the daughter of a prominent man from an old Bluenose family, grew up in Bolingbroke, Nova Scotia. She met Anne Shirley and Priscilla Grant at Old St. John's Cemetery while starting her studies at Redmond College, quickly adopting them as friends and introducing them into Redmond's social circle. When Anne and Priscilla secured the lease for Patty's Place, Phil excitedly joined their housekeeping arrangement. During a summer stay at a boardinghouse, she met a divinity student named Jonas Blake, whose sermon deeply moved her and made her realize she had fallen in love with him. She later accepted Jonas's marriage proposal, confiding her decision to Anne. After graduating from Redmond College, Phil comforted Anne following her rejection of Roy Gardner's proposal. Shortly after completing her studies, Phil was married, with Anne serving as her bridesmaid.

unit: Phil Gordon, the daughter of a prominent man from an old Bluenose family, grew up in Bolingbroke, Nova Scotia. She met Anne Shirley and Priscilla Grant at Old St. John's Cemetery while starting her studies at Redmond College, quickly adopting them as friends and introducing them into Redmond's social circle. When Anne and Priscilla secured the lease for Patty's Place, Phil excitedly joined their housekeeping arrangement. During a summer stay at a boardinghouse, she met a divinity student named Jonas Blake, whose sermon deeply moved her and made her realize she had fallen in love with him. She later accepted Jonas's marriage proposal, confiding her decision to Anne. After graduating from Redmond College, Phil comforted Anne following her rejection of Roy Gardner's proposal. Shortly after completing her studies, Phil was married, with Anne serving as her bridesmaid.

label: Quote
value: Phil Gordon said: "I’ll go, if I can walk with Priscilla and Charlie. That will be a bearable degree of gooseberry. That Gilbert of yours is a darling, Anne, but why does he go around so much with Goggle-eyes?"

label: Quote
value: Phil Gordon said: "I don’t want William’s Island especially, but I’m sure I couldn’t get it if I did. Look at that sentry on the summit of the fort, right beside the flag. Doesn’t he look as if he had stepped out of a romance?"

label: Quote
value: Phil Gordon said: "Look—in white letters, around the archway over the gate. ‘Patty’s Place.’ Isn’t that killing? Especially on this Avenue of Pinehursts and Elmwolds and Cedarcrofts? ‘Patty’s Place,’ if you please! I adore it."

label: Quote
value: Phil Gordon said: "Joseph, you calico beastie, don’t you dare jump on my lap. I won’t go to a dance all over cat hairs. No, Anne, I won’t look matronly. But no doubt I’ll be married."

label: Quote
value: Phil Gordon said: "No, he would do if he wasn’t poor. I must marry a rich man, Aunt Jamesina. That—and good looks—is an indispensable qualification. I’d marry Gilbert Blythe if he were rich."

value: Phillips is a local schoolteacher.
unit: As a local schoolteacher who boarded at Eben Wright's house, Phillips was known for frequently whipping his students and maintaining poor order in his classroom. When Gilbert Blythe teased Anne Shirley, prompting her to smash her slate over Gilbert's head, Phillips punished Anne by making her stand at the blackboard. Later, Phillips publicly disciplined Anne for being late by forcing her to sit next to Gilbert, an act that drove Anne to temporarily quit attending his school.

label: History
value: Priscilla Grant attended Queen's Academy
unit: Priscilla Grant attended Queen's Academy alongside Anne Shirley and was the niece of author Mrs. Charlotte E. Morgan. During a spring picnic walk, Priscilla joined her friends in naming Crystal Lake and poeticizing nature while exploring Hester Gray's garden. She later surprised Anne by bringing Mrs. Morgan to Green Gables for an unexpected visit. Priscilla reunited with Anne in Kingsport, taking her to their boardinghouse before registering together at Redmond College. The two girls met Philippa Gordon in Old St.

value: Roy Gardner said: "That ought to be sufficient introduction. My name is Royal Gardner. And you are the Miss Shirley who read the Tennyson paper at the Philomathic the other evening, aren’t you?"

label: Quote
value: Roy Gardner said: "I feel as if I didn’t belong anywhere yet. I put in my Freshman and Sophomore years at Redmond two years ago. I’ve been in Europe ever since. Now I’ve come back to finish my Arts course."

label: Quote
value: Roy Gardner said: "I can’t understand it—I can’t believe you are not the woman I’ve believed you to be. But reproaches are idle between us. You are the only woman I can ever love. I thank you for your friendship, at least. Good-bye, Anne."

label: History
value: Ruby Gillis grew up with many big sisters.
unit: Ruby Gillis grew up with many big sisters and once used a magic pebble to charm away her warts. During her school days, she formed a Story Club alongside Anne and Jane Andrews. Ruby expressed a childhood wish to have dozens of beaus when she grew up, and she visited Boston the fall before falling ill. During Anne's time at Redmond, Ruby sent updates from home in a bundle of letters. After Anne returned to Avonlea, she learned that Ruby was terminally ill with consumption, even though Ruby stubbornly insisted she was healthy during a visit at her home. Later, Ruby tearfully confessed her fear of dying to Anne during an evening together, but she passed away peacefully in her sleep the following night.

value: Ruby Gillis said: "Me! Why, I’m perfectly well. I never felt better in my life. Of course, that congestion last winter pulled me down a little. But just see my color. I don’t look much like an invalid, I’m sure."

label: Quote
value: Ruby Gillis said: "Anne, it won’t be long now before I’ll be lying over there. You and Diana and all the rest will be going about, full of life—and I’ll be there—in the old graveyard—dead!"

label: Quote
value: Ruby Gillis said: "I’ll try. I’ll think over what you have said, and try to believe it. And you’ll come up as often as you can, won’t you, Anne?"

label: Quote
value: Ruby Gillis said: “Nor I,” said Ruby Gillis, with a shiver. “I don’t mind floating down when there’s two or three of us in the flat and we can sit up. It’s fun then. But to lie down and pretend I was dead—I just couldn’t. I’d die really of fright.”

Upon returning to Green Gables, she was shocked to learn that Gilbert was critically ill with typhoid fever, spending a grief-stricken night realizing her deep love for him before learning at dawn that he had survived the crisis.

During her college years, Stella lived at Patty's Place with her friends, chatting about household matters and simple living alongside Aunt Jamesina and Phil. In her final year at Redmond, she reminisced with Anne over old Story Club manuscripts during a rainy evening of studying. Following final examinations, Stella and her housemates gathered to reflect on the life lessons and common sense they gained over their four years at college before packing up to leave Patty's Place after graduation.

label: Quote
value: Stella Maynard said: "I love Anne and I like Roy. Everybody says she is making a brilliant match, and even Mrs. Gardner thinks her charming now. It all sounds as if it were made in heaven, but I have my doubts. Make the most of that, Aunt Jamesina."

label: Quote
value: Stella Maynard said: “Well, I don’t know how he and the Sarah-cat will ever make out to live together,” said Stella pesimistically. “Cat-fights in the orchard o’nights are bad enough. But cat-fights here in the livingroom are unthinkable.”

label: Quote
value: Stella Maynard said: "I was afraid they’d come back. And then our jolly little nest here would be broken up—and we poor callow nestlings thrown out on the cruel world of boardinghouses again."

label: Quote
value: Stella Maynard said: "Nothing seems worthwhile. My very thoughts are old. I’ve thought them all before. What is the use of living after all, Anne?"

label: Quote
value: Stella Maynard said: "Oh, my mind agrees with you, Anne. But my soul remains doleful and uninspired. I’m always grubby and dingy on rainy nights."

Despite an initial wave of severe stage fright upon seeing the sophisticated crowd and high-caliber performers, Anne sees Gilbert Blythe in the audience and finds the resolve to deliver a triumphant recitation, earning an encore and praise from the guests.

value: Anne stays in Bolingbroke with Phil Gordon.
chapter: v3 · Chapter XXI Roses of Yesterday
unit: During her stay in Bolingbroke with Phil Gordon, Anne visits her humble birthplace and meets the woman currently living there. The woman allows Anne to explore the house, including the room where she was born, and hands over a small packet of old letters written by Anne's parents. Anne later visits her parents' grave and reads the letters, feeling for the first time that she truly knows them.

label: v2 · II Selling in Haste and Repenting at Leisure
value: Anne and Diana discuss Village Improvement Society plans.
chapter: v2 · II Selling in Haste and Repenting at Leisure
unit: Anne and Diana discuss Village Improvement Society plans on their drive home from Carmody when they spot a Jersey cow trampling Mr. Harrison's oat field. Believing the cow is her own nuisance Jersey, Dolly, Anne impulsively sells the stray cow on the spot to Mr. Shearer for twenty dollars. Upon returning to Green Gables, Anne discovers Dolly still in the barnyard and realizes she accidentally sold Mr. Harrison's cow, prompting her to head over to his house with the money and a cake to confess.

value: Anne returns to Avonlea
chapter: v3 · Chapter XI The Round of Life
unit: Anne returns to Avonlea and learns from Mrs. Lynde that Ruby Gillis is terminally ill with consumption. On their way to visit Ruby, Anne and Diana stop at the Wrights' house, where Aunt Atossa makes several unpleasant comments, after which Anne reveals to Diana her plans to write a short story. They then visit the Gillis household, finding a lively crowd and Ruby stubbornly insisting she is perfectly healthy despite her failing condition.

unit: Anne and Diana discuss Village Improvement Society plans on their drive home from Carmody when they spot a Jersey cow trampling Mr. Harrison's oat field. Believing the cow is her own nuisance Jersey, Dolly, Anne impulsively sells the stray cow on the spot to Mr. Shearer for twenty dollars. Upon returning to Green Gables, Anne discovers Dolly still in the barnyard and realizes she accidentally sold Mr. Harrison's cow, prompting her to head over to his house with the money and a cake to confess.

unit: On the eve of the school term, Anne discusses teaching methods and classroom discipline with Jane and Gilbert, strongly opposing corporal punishment. After returning to Green Gables, she visits Mr. Harrison, who also doubts her plan to rule by affection rather than the rod. The next morning, a nervous Anne drinks ginger tea prepared by Marilla before starting her first day of teaching.

unit: Marilla returns home to Green Gables expecting supper, but finds the stove unlit and Anne nowhere in sight. After washing fails to remove the green color, Marilla cuts Anne's hair off short, leaving Anne to reflect remorsefully on her vanity.

chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XXXVIII. The Bend in the Road
unit: Marilla learns from an oculist that she must give up heavy eye work or face total blindness, putting the future of Green Gables in jeopardy. Anne decides to forfeit her college scholarship, stay at home to care for Marilla, and take up a local teaching job instead. After learning Gilbert Blythe gave up the Avonlea school so she could have it, Anne meets Gilbert on her way home and they finally end their feud to become close friends.

chapter: v2 · II Selling in Haste and Repenting at Leisure
unit: Anne and Diana discuss Village Improvement Society plans on their drive home from Carmody when they spot a Jersey cow trampling Mr. Harrison's oat field. Believing the cow is her own nuisance Jersey, Dolly, Anne impulsively sells the stray cow on the spot to Mr. Shearer for twenty dollars. Upon returning to Green Gables, Anne discovers Dolly still in the barnyard and realizes she accidentally sold Mr. Harrison's cow, prompting her to head over to his house with the money and a cake to confess.

He seeks help from Mrs. Lynde, who agrees to buy and sew a stylish brown dress with puffed sleeves for Anne. On Christmas morning, Anne is overjoyed to receive the dress from Matthew, along with a pair of slippers sent by Aunt Josephine.

value: Marilla returns home to Green Gables.
chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XXVII. Vanity and Vexation of Spirit
unit: Marilla returns home to Green Gables expecting supper, but finds the stove unlit and Anne nowhere in sight. When Marilla goes upstairs, she discovers Anne hiding under her pillows because she dyed her red hair green using hair dye bought from a peddler. After washing fails to remove the green color, Marilla cuts Anne's hair off short, leaving Anne to reflect remorsefully on her vanity.

The next day, after learning that Miss Barry is furious and threatening to cut off Diana's music lessons, Anne expresses her remorse to Mrs. Lynde.

label: v2 · II Selling in Haste and Repenting at Leisure
value: Anne and Diana discuss Village Improvement Society plans.
chapter: v2 · II Selling in Haste and Repenting at Leisure
unit: Anne and Diana discuss Village Improvement Society plans on their drive home from Carmody when they spot a Jersey cow trampling Mr. Harrison's oat field. Believing the cow is her own nuisance Jersey, Dolly, Anne impulsively sells the stray cow on the spot to Mr. Shearer for twenty dollars. Upon returning to Green Gables, Anne discovers Dolly still in the barnyard and realizes she accidentally sold Mr. Harrison's cow, prompting her to head over to his house with the money and a cake to confess.

unit: On the eve of the school term, Anne discusses teaching methods and classroom discipline with Jane and Gilbert, strongly opposing corporal punishment. After returning to Green Gables, she visits Mr. Harrison, who also doubts her plan to rule by affection rather than the rod. The next morning, a nervous Anne drinks ginger tea prepared by Marilla before starting her first day of teaching.

value: Anne returns to Avonlea

unit: Anne returns to Avonlea and learns from Mrs. Lynde that Ruby Gillis is terminally ill with consumption. On their way to visit Ruby, Anne and Diana stop at the Wrights' house, where Aunt Atossa makes several unpleasant comments, after which Anne reveals to Diana her plans to write a short story. They then visit the Gillis household, finding a lively crowd and Ruby stubbornly insisting she is perfectly healthy despite her failing condition.

value: Anne discusses teaching methods with Jane and Gilbert.
chapter: v2 · IV Different Opinions
unit: On the eve of the school term, Anne discusses teaching methods and classroom discipline with Jane and Gilbert, strongly opposing corporal punishment. After returning to Green Gables, she visits Mr. Harrison, who also doubts her plan to rule by affection rather than the rod. The next morning, a nervous Anne drinks ginger tea prepared by Marilla before starting her first day of teaching.

label: v2 · VI All Sorts and Conditions of Men . . . and women
value: Anne and Diana continue canvassing Avonlea for subscriptions
chapter: v2 · VI All Sorts and Conditions of Men . . . and women
unit: Anne and Diana continue canvassing Avonlea for subscriptions, encountering peculiar neighbors like the hyper-neat Mrs. Theodore White and receiving mixed results. Learning that Lorenzo White just had a new baby boy, Anne strategically visits him while he is overjoyed, securing a generous five-dollar donation. Later that evening, Anne visits Mr. Harrison to ask for a contribution, but he flatly refuses.

label: v2 · II Selling in Haste and Repenting at Leisure
value: Anne and Diana discuss Village Improvement Society plans.
chapter: v2 · II Selling in Haste and Repenting at Leisure
unit: Anne and Diana discuss Village Improvement Society plans on their drive home from Carmody when they spot a Jersey cow trampling Mr. Harrison's oat field. Believing the cow is her own nuisance Jersey, Dolly, Anne impulsively sells the stray cow on the spot to Mr. Shearer for twenty dollars. Upon returning to Green Gables, Anne discovers Dolly still in the barnyard and realizes she accidentally sold Mr. Harrison's cow, prompting her to head over to his house with the money and a cake to confess.

unit: Marilla learns from an oculist that she must give up heavy eye work or face total blindness, putting the future of Green Gables in jeopardy. chapter: v2 · II Selling in Haste and Repenting at Leisure
unit: Anne and Diana discuss Village Improvement Society plans on their drive home from Carmody when they spot a Jersey cow trampling Mr. Harrison's oat field. Believing the cow is her own nuisance Jersey, Dolly, Anne impulsively sells the stray cow on the spot to Mr. Shearer for twenty dollars. Upon returning to Green Gables, Anne discovers Dolly still in the barnyard and realizes she accidentally sold Mr. Harrison's cow, prompting her to head over to his house with the money and a cake to confess.
